# Build a cloud small enough to hold in your head 🔴

**Goal.** Assemble the smallest honest cloud: microVMs that boot in a tenth of a second, one L2 they share with a QEMU VM and a rootless container, a real 169.254.169.254 served by a process you started, a control plane that reconciles declared against derived, backups that can say what built them, and a fleet of warm clones from one memory image. Every step is a command you type; the wizard is only a view of it.

**Audience:** you have booted a VM and run a container; now find out what a cloud adds on top of them  
**Effort:** ⏱ half-day+  
**Prerequisites:** [Containers from first principles](path-container-internals.md) · [Chroot → running system: the cross-phase bridges](path-chroot-to-system.md)

| # | Lab | You'll learn | Checkpoint (observable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | one Firecracker microVM by hand — a config.json, a kernel, an ext4 rootfs, and the REST socket the VMM serves. Nothing here is a tool yet. | a login prompt at ~0.55 s, and the same boot again over the API with `curl` — RUNBOOK-first-microvm.md. |
| 2 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | the microVM gets an identity: MMDS v2 at 169.254.169.254, with the token handshake EC2 taught you, served by the process you started. | `instance-id` read INSIDE the guest matches the host's PUT; the same GET without a token returns 401. |
| 3 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | the fabric — one bridge, addressless taps, dnsmasq as DHCP and DNS — built ADDITIVELY beside whatever already owns your host's networking. | `api1` pings `api2` BY NAME; teardown asserts the absence of our objects only, and the host's own tunnel binding is unmoved. |
| 4 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | the tool, and what it hides: `lab-fc.sh` generates that config and babysits the process, and every field it fills in for you is reported. | `lab-fc.sh mac api1` prints a MAC DERIVED from the name — the same value `fabric.sh mac` must produce, or the guest misses its DHCP reservation silently; and `create --config … --dry-run` prints the config plus a provenance table naming every value you did not type.<br>🔎 auto-checkable → marker `06:00:ac:47` 🖥️ |
| 5 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | a second engine on one fabric: QEMU `-M microvm` booting the SAME kernel and the SAME rootfs, so the only variable left is the VMM. | a boot-time number with its spread — and the surprise that 90% of Firecracker's canonical figure was a PS/2 probe. |
| 6 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | vsock — the first channel that is not the fabric. One static guest agent, two host APIs that differ in kind. | the same guest record shape from both engines, with no bridge, no tap and no root. |
| 7 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | the control plane: declared versus derived, and a diff that holds back the kinds it must not act on. | `apply` is a no-op on pass two because the DIFF finds nothing — not because a flag was remembered. |
| 8 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | preserve: two tiers and a derivation, so a backup can say what built it. | change ONE byte of a saved artifact and the restore refuses BY NAME, with both digests, before importing anything — RUNBOOK-preserve.md. |
| 9 | [`micro-cloud`](../micro-cloud/) | the fleet: five warm clones from ONE memory image, and the identity that comes back with them. | all five resume the captured tick rather than booting, share one unchanged mem file — and all five share one boot_id, which is the lesson — RUNBOOK-fleet.md. |
